what_this_is: The SECOND independent revalidation of the ten complete five-link chains (plus the designated target Level::is_zero) against a MOVED producer. The first, recorded in data/crystal_chain_revalidation_2026-08-19.json, used trust origin/main 6819d58406. This one uses trust origin/main ccf52b40c3 -- 33 commits later, including three PRODUCER-ADOPTION vtable slices (13, 14, 15) and the call-arg/nonmax arm. The IR-emitting lowering itself moved: crates/trust-ir-bridge/src/lower.rs c0cda7b988 -> 083c00091c.

supersedes.relationship: CONFIRMS AND EXTENDS -- it does not overwrite and nothing in it is retracted.
supersedes.reproduced_first: Before measuring anything new, scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py was run against the EARLIER lane's own dump (l2dz/dump_O3). It reproduced that record exactly: 11/11 verdicts, 11/11 drift-class sets, and 11/11 at_head lineage digests. The earlier record is faithful to the dump it was taken from.

the_risk_this_tested: Each chain pins its body's emitted trust-ir VERBATIM as a committed fixture, and link 2a is a CFG gate asserting the registered spec module encodes that same graph. The gate reads the FIXTURE. If the producer stopped emitting what the fixture records, every link-2a gate would keep passing while the shipped kernel was built from something else. Several producer waves have landed since the first revalidation, so the question had to be asked again.
the_answer: NO CHAINED BODY DRIFTED. Zero instructions moved in any of the eleven; every instr_count is identical (10/14/27/6/13/15/26/2/2/9, is_zero at 28); no `gep` was added to any body. One body (has_cubical_layer) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its fixture; the other ten differ only in whole-crate NUMBERING indices, the same four classes the first revalidation classified. All ten chains hold links 1/2b/2c at HEAD -- agreed, markers_exact true, unsupported [], zero calls, flip fired. Level::is_zero is unchanged: agreed, markers_exact FALSE, NO flip event, 6 resolved calls. The wall stands.
the_sharper_result_this_run_adds: LINEAGE IS STABLE ACROSS TWO INDEPENDENT PRODUCER GENERATIONS. The first revalidation measured that the chained bodies move in func_id ALONE across ONE producer step. This run measures the same thing across a much larger one: over 13,076 common coverage rows, 5,568 moved, 51 of them in instr_count (net +368 instructions) and 154 in `lineage` -- and all ELEVEN chained bodies moved in func_id alone. Not instr_count, not lowered/spliced/unsupported/calls, and NOT lineage. So every chained body's lineage digest and def_index at HEAD are the values the earlier record already pinned, and NO LINEAGE RE-PIN IS REQUIRED. That is a stronger statement than the first run could make, and it is the one that decides whether the link-2c pins are stale: they are not.
what_DID_move: Whole-crate NUMBERING, and by more than last time: functy.N on all ten chains (e.g. kind_ord 470 -> 306), enum.N/struct.N on three, @func.N on is_zero (4914 -> 3885). These renumber whenever the producer changes how many bodies it lowers. They are read by no gate lane, and ir_ty_is_agg_enum_any / ir_ty_is_agg_struct_any (spec/core_spec/eval_ir_ops.rs) PROVE ir_ty_is_agg (IRTy.enum_ n) = Bool.true for every n, so a type index cannot reach the value the machine computes. func_id moved by 2-3 on every chained body.
why_the_fixtures_are_NOT_refreshed: Refreshing was tried and measured by the first lane and the result stands: it takes crystal_a1_lineage from 59/59 to 57 passed / 2 failed, because expr_path_step_clone's const-type lane and level_is_zero.rs's hard-coded callee assertion spell the OLD indices. Re-recording a whole-crate ordinal that renumbers on every producer change would be stale again next wave -- and this run is the evidence for that: those indices moved AGAIN, by more than last time, while not one instruction did. The fixture pins the BODY; the body has not moved.
what_still_nothing_checks: Re-derivation remains a MANUAL duty. Verified independently at f0846ade2: the only trustc-invoking scripts in this repo are trust_ir_build.sh, trust_verify_ratchet.sh, check_trustcore_evidence_staleness.py, trust_ir_axes.py, local_gate.sh and test_isabelle_ops_portability.py, and NOT ONE of them reads a *.trust-ir.txt fixture (grepped). scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py is referenced by no gate, no hook (core.hooksPath = .git/hooks), no justfile recipe and no verify_runner row -- tests/crystal_a1_lineage/freshness.rs reads its SOURCE to check coverage, it does not RUN it. So nothing SCHEDULES the comparison; what the 2026-08-19 mechanism guarantees is that when it is run, its result is committed and cross-checked, and that no chain can exist without an entry. The gap named in freshness.rs -- data/ and scripts/ are outside verify_runner's input digest -- is still open and is still correctly named there.

(2) Against the FIRST revalidation's driver (6819d58406) selftest is UNPROVEN -- both register the identical class set, so that discriminator cannot tell them apart, and 'could not distinguish' is not 'identical'. Identification there is BY OUTPUT DIGEST and by source: the two drivers emit DIFFERENT artifacts from byte-identical clean-kernel source (coverage.json eb11159a... vs the first record's 0e186763..., trust-ir.txt 0130c769... vs bddb9b9b...), and three producer source blobs moved (lower.rs, differential.rs, crate_module.rs).

The SOURCE is ccf52b40c3, recorded in seal-l3rv/{REV,PROVENANCE} and evidenced as above.
